title: Remove a damaged robot-cover screw
instruction: Remove the damaged screw from the robot's cable cover.
justification: A real Mitsubishi RH-2FRH robot service cover, original mounted orientation and M4x6 stainless button-head fastener. This is robot maintenance hardware, not a generic plate relabeled as AI equipment.
fault: The 2.5 mm hex recess has been rounded to a 3.0 mm cylindrical recess, preserving the original exterior head and threads. Reset must specify this machining and installation procedure; no rust, adhesive or seizure is claimed.
objects: Full-scale RH-2FRH2515 envelope on its ordinary bolted base; original cable cover and other three cover screws retained. Loose ENGINEER PZ-58 extraction pliers, original 160 mm length, 130 g mass, spring-loaded handles. Standard 2.5 mm key and replacement M4x6 gauge screw are final-task requirements, not yet implemented.
skill: Establish and maintain external serrated-jaw engagement on a shallow rounded head while applying removal torque; permit external pliers, internal extractors and safe direct-grasp routes if they physically work. Neither a named tool nor two arms is mandatory.
scoring: Current diagnostic always scores zero. Proposed complete task: removed screw outside the original threaded hole, cover intact, replacement gauge screw threads through original attachment. Rotation alone is not full recovery. Partial credit still requires a practical axial-backout measure.

nearest.difference: Impact driver on seized automotive rotor screws. Here the fault is a rounded drive interface on actual robot hardware, without invented seizure, detached horizontal plate or rotation-only completion.
Socket engagement with intact hex head and confined ratcheting. External gripping of a shallow rounded head is a different contact problem, but generic screw turning remains shared.
Reversed ratchet direction did not change the core skill; this task cannot rely on the recovery narrative or robot label alone.
Prepared screw puller turns a pre-engaged screw to extract a collar; tool engagement on a damaged fastener is absent. Its rejection warns that screw rotation alone is saturated.

risks: Native 50 N-per-finger grip may not transmit the actual 1.39–1.89 Nm installation-load scale through these short plier jaws.
The maker specifies fixing torque, not a measured breakaway torque; the prototype must not silently equate the two as calibration.
Serration microgeometry and friction are estimates; no artificial attachment or invented plastic cutting is allowed.
Complete physical thread withdrawal and gauge-screw assay remain unimplemented.
Robot envelope is dimensioned; cover placement and small noncritical details are photo estimates, disclosed and kept in the original orientation.
No final novelty clearance or acceptance claim.
decision: Build one bounded native grasp/contact gate; approximately 0.2 review prospect, conditional on physical engagement and full recovery, not final clearance.
